messages:
maria: Heads up — customer (acme-corp) on Private VPC reported missing audit logs after 2026-03-15T22:03Z and intermittent KMS 403s for Decrypt. They also surface DLP alerts for outbound uploads to a third-party S3 proxy. Can someone triage?
ryan: @maria thanks. Do we have a customer packet with config, NAT IPs, and a few sample request ids? 403 suggests KMS policy or egress block.
kevin: Asking customer for ids now. quick checklist: firewall rules (egress), DNS/proxy settings, KMS key policy, and any HSM rotation windows.
security-bot: Alert: DLP rule "external-s3-upload" triggered 6 times in the last hour for acme-corp (rule_id: dlpr-42). Linked evidence: https://dlp.internal/acme-corp/evt/2345
jess: Two quick notes — (1) Private deploys can have audit retention set per-customer; if retention accidentally set to 0 it looks like logs are rotated immediately. (2) KMS 403s often correlate with egress or TLS SNI rewrite through customer proxies.
ops-oncall: I pulled the customer's firewall policy: default-deny outbound, allowlist contains only aws-commercial ranges, no internal KMS/HSM ranges configured. Suspect egress blocked for KMS hostname kms.acme.internal -> 10.11.0.5 (private resolver).
ryan: Can ops-oncall attach the firewall ACL snapshot and a packet capture from one of the failing nodes? A tcpdump around the time of a 403 will help. Example tcpdump filter: `tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.11.0.5 and port 443 -w /tmp/kms-403.pcap`
kevin: Also get the redwood agent logs on the private node: `/var/log/redwood/agent.log` — grep for the request id and `kms:Decrypt`. Sample: 
```
2026-03-15T22:02:57Z ERROR request_id=abc123 kms:Decrypt failed status=403 endpoint=kms.acme.internal:443
```

maria: Customer provided one request id: abc123 and a tcpdump. Uploading shortly. They say the proxy rewrites SNI and strips some headers for egress filtering.
ops-oncall: Got the pcap. TLS handshake completes but the server responds with `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden` on the POST to /decrypt. The TCP connection is to 10.11.0.5:443 which then forwards to their proxy. Looks like proxy returns 403 before hitting KMS.
jess: That matches SNI/header stripping. KMS expects client certs or specific Host/SNI for HSM-backed keys. If proxy replaces SNI, HSM may reject. We should confirm if the customer is using HSM-wrapped keys (kms:KeySpec=HSM).
kevin: Ask customer to run a direct test bypassing the proxy (if possible) from a bastion in their VPC: 
```
curl -v https://kms.acme.internal/decrypt -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"CiphertextBlob":"..."}'
```
If that returns 200 then proxy is the culprit.
security-bot: Runbook link: https://runbooks.internal/vpc-kms-proxy-triage (steps: collect pcap, agent logs, firewall ACL, DNS resolution, SNI check).
ryan: Action items: 1) ops-oncall attach firewall ACL export + pcap (done) 2) customer to attempt direct curl from bastion 3) jess check key metadata for HSM policy 4) kevin prepare temporary allowlist rule for kms host if proxy can't be changed.
ops-oncall: Added suggestion to customer: add outbound allow rule for kms.acme.internal (tcp/443) to NAT gateway IPs and whitelist in proxy. If they can't change proxy, we can offer to support a flow-through via dedicated egress IPs (requires config + security review).
maria: Customer confirmed they can run the curl test; they'll try and report back. Also asked if audit retention could explain missing logs — they didn't change retention knowingly.
jess: I'll check the control plane — looks like retention config for acme-corp was set to 0 by an infra script rollback on 2026-03-15 21:58 UTC. That explains the missing logs. I'm restoring to 90d now and will backfill available logs into the retention store if possible.
kevin: Good catch. So two separate but related issues: (A) audit retention misconfigured -> logs rotated, (B) proxy/SNI causing KMS 403s and DLP alerts.
ryan: If customer needs immediate unblocking for decrypts we can (with approvals) add a temporary policy to route KMS traffic to a managed egress IP we control, bypassing their proxy for that host. Ops, can you estimate how fast we can provision?
ops-oncall: We can provision a temporary egress NAT and update routing in ~2 hours after approval. Will need ticket and customer sign-off.
maria: I'll coordinate customer approval. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
kevin: Noted - I'll draft a short remediation checklist to send to customer (firewall allowlist entry, proxy SNI passthrough, restore retention, optional temp egress).
jess: I filed infra rollback issue: infra-1248 to prevent retention rollbacks.
security-bot: Case updated: acme-corp escalation -> state: investigating, severity: high.
maria: Closing loop once customer confirms curl + retention backfill. Leaving thread open.
